title: Preventing PostgreSQL XID Wraparound Outages & Autovacuum Starvation

spark.summary: Harden a 400 GB PostgreSQL ledger handling 30,000 updates/sec against 5x MVCC table bloat and emergency 2B XID wraparound write freezes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Eliminate xmin pinners with 30s idle-in-transaction timeouts and max_slot_keep_wal_size, enable fillfactor=70 HOT updates, and raise autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit to 2000.
spark.byteSummary:
In Production Scenario #28, a 400 GB PostgreSQL ledger sustaining 30,000 updates/sec suffered 5x table bloat followed by an emergency 2B XID wraparound write shutdown. Root-cause analysis revealed two compounding failures: an idle `BEGIN; SELECT` reporting transaction pinning the global `xmin` horizon, and default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` throttling freeze workers far below the XID burn rate.

At 30,000 write XIDs/sec, a cluster burns through 2 billion XIDs in under 19 hours if freezing stalls. Every non-HOT update also amplified B-tree index writes, saturating disk I/O.

The hardened production architecture enforces `fillfactor=70` for page-local HOT updates, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s`, `max_slot_keep_wal_size` to drop dead replication slots, `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000` across parallel freeze workers, and tiered XID-age alerting—holding table bloat below 5% with zero write freezes.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: Incident Anatomy — 30K/s Ledger & Emergency Write Freeze
learningJourney.purpose: Trace how 30,000 updates/sec combined with pinned xmin and throttled autovacuum drives a 400 GB ledger to a read-only halt.
learningJourney.explanation: At 30,000 write XIDs/sec, PostgreSQL consumes ~108M XIDs per hour and hits the 2B wraparound limit in ~18.5 hours if `relfrozenxid` cannot advance. Meanwhile, unreclaimed dead tuples inflate a 400 GB table to 2 TB (5x bloat), degrading buffer-cache hit ratios and slowing every sequential/index scan until the emergency shutdown triggers.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: Live Triage Queries (pg_stat_activity & pg_class)
learningJourney.purpose: Identify the exact oldest relfrozenxid tables, idle-in-transaction blockers, and inactive replication slots during an incident.
learningJourney.explanation: During an active XID-age spike, operators must immediately rank tables by `age(relfrozenxid)` in `pg_class` and cross-reference `pg_stat_activity` for `backend_xmin` holders and `pg_replication_slots` for inactive `xmin`/`catalog_xmin` pins. Terminating a single zombie PID via `pg_terminate_backend(pid)` unblocks autovacuum within seconds.

sectionDiagram.title: Three-Query Incident Triage to Unpin Global xmin

cards.label: Check Subtransactions
cards.detail: Monitor pg_stat_activity wait events for SubtransSLRU contention alongside backend_xmin.

cards.label: Safe Slot Drop
cards.detail: Verify consumer replica is decommissioned before calling pg_drop_replication_slot().

sectionDiagram.summary: Inspecting pg_class, pg_stat_activity, and pg_replication_slots pinpoints the exact blocker holding back relfrozenxid.
sectionDiagram.caption: Operators query pg_class, pg_stat_activity, and pg_replication_slots to locate and terminate xmin blockers.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: Enforcing Session Timeouts & Replication WAL Caps
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent future xmin pinning automatically using 30s idle-in-transaction timeouts and max_slot_keep_wal_size.
learningJourney.explanation: Manual triage is too slow at 30K XIDs/sec. Setting `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '30s'` and `statement_timeout = '15s'` on OLTP/reporting roles automatically aborts forgotten `BEGIN; SELECT` sessions. Setting `max_slot_keep_wal_size = '20GB'` invalidates disconnected replication slots before they pin xmin or fill pg_wal.

sectionDiagram.title: Automated Guardrails Against Zombie Sessions & Dead Slots

cards.label: Replica Read Isolation
cards.detail: Route long-running BI analytics to a dedicated read replica without hot_standby_feedback.

cards.label: PgBouncer Transaction Pooling
cards.detail: Transaction-mode pooling returns connections immediately after COMMIT, reducing idle-in-tx risk.

sectionDiagram.summary: 30-second idle-in-transaction timeouts and max_slot_keep_wal_size prevent zombie sessions and dead slots from pinning xmin.
sectionDiagram.caption: 30s idle-in-transaction timeouts and 20 GB max_slot_keep_wal_size keep the global xmin horizon unpinned.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: HOT Updates with fillfactor=70 on Update-Heavy Tables
learningJourney.purpose: Keep 30,000 updates/sec page-local and hold table bloat under 5% using fillfactor=70.
learningJourney.explanation: On the 400 GB ledger, setting `ALTER TABLE ledger SET (fillfactor = 70);` reserves 30% free space on every 8 KB heap page. Non-indexed column updates stay on the same heap page as Heap-Only Tuples (HOT), eliminating secondary B-tree index writes and allowing inline page pruning to keep steady-state bloat under 5%.

sectionDiagram.title: fillfactor=70 + Inline Page Pruning for < 5% Bloat

cards.label: REPACK / pg_repack
cards.detail: Existing 5x-bloated tables require online pg_repack (or VACUUM FULL) after setting fillfactor=70 to rewrite dense pages.

cards.label: Index Column Hygiene
cards.detail: Avoid indexing monotonically updated timestamp/counter columns that would disqualify HOT updates.

sectionDiagram.summary: Reserving 30% free space per page with fillfactor=70 enables HOT updates and inline pruning, holding bloat under 5%.
sectionDiagram.caption: fillfactor=70 reserves 2,457 bytes per 8 KB page for HOT updates and inline pruning, capping bloat below 5%.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Autovacuum Cost-Limit & Worker Scaling
learningJourney.purpose: Configure autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000 and multi-worker parallelism so freezing outpaces XID burn.
learningJourney.explanation: Default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` caps vacuum at ~8 MB/s per worker—far too slow for a 400 GB table at 30K updates/sec. Increasing `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000` (with `cost_delay=2ms`), lowering `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.01`, and setting `autovacuum_max_workers=6` gives freeze workers 10x I/O throughput without starving OLTP queries.

sectionDiagram.title: 10x Autovacuum I/O Budget & Scale-Factor Tuning

cards.label: Shared Cost Balance
cards.detail: Remember autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit is shared across active workers unless overridden per table.

cards.label: maintenance_work_mem
cards.detail: Set maintenance_work_mem=1GB..2GB so VACUUM stores dead-tuple TIDs in 1 pass instead of multiple index scans.

sectionDiagram.summary: Tuning cost_limit=2000, scale_factor=0.01, and maintenance_work_mem=1GB lets autovacuum keep pace with 30K updates/sec.
sectionDiagram.caption: Early 0.01 scale_factor triggers, cost_limit=2000, and 6 workers maintain relfrozenxid < 200M.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: Partitioning & Subtransaction Avoidance at 30K/s
learningJourney.purpose: Bound freeze scan blast radius via time-based partitioning and avoid SubtransSLRU XID amplification.
learningJourney.explanation: Vacuuming a monolithic 400 GB table takes hours even with tuned I/O; range-partitioning by day or week limits active vacuuming to ~20 GB hot partitions while cold partitions stay 100% all-frozen in the Visibility Map. Additionally, eliminating nested `SAVEPOINT` / PL/pgSQL `EXCEPTION` blocks avoids subtransaction XID burn and SubtransSLRU lock contention.

sectionDiagram.title: Bounding Freeze Blast Radius with Partitioned Hot Tables

cards.label: 95% I/O Reduction
cards.detail: Partitioning shrinks active freeze scans from 400 GB to a 20 GB hot partition (~4.3 minutes).

cards.label: Subtransaction Trap
cards.detail: A single transaction with 1,000 SAVEPOINTs burns 1,000 XIDs and can trigger SubtransSLRU stalls.

sectionDiagram.summary: Range partitioning shrinks freeze scans from 400 GB to 20 GB hot partitions while avoiding SAVEPOINT XID amplification.
sectionDiagram.caption: Weekly partitioning isolates 20 GB hot writes from 380 GB all-frozen cold partitions, cutting freeze time to ~4 minutes.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Tiered XID-Age Alerting & Single-User Emergency Runbook
learningJourney.purpose: Catch wraparound risk 10+ hours early via Prometheus telemetry and document safe single-user VACUUM FREEZE recovery.
learningJourney.explanation: Export `max(age(relfrozenxid))` and `max(age(datfrozenxid))` every 60 seconds with alerts at 150M (info), 500M (page on-call), and 1.5B (critical). If a cluster ever reaches the 2B read-only wall, stop application pools, start `postgres --single -D $PGDATA <db>`, execute `VACUUM FREEZE;`, and restart normal multi-user service.

sectionDiagram.title: Tiered XID-Age Alerting & Single-User Emergency Thaw

cards.label: Database-Wide datfrozenxid
cards.detail: Remember pg_database.datfrozenxid tracks the oldest relfrozenxid across all tables—even unused template0/postgres DBs.

cards.label: Pre-Freeze Verification
cards.detail: Confirm disk space headroom before running VACUUM FREEZE so WAL generation does not fill $PGDATA.

sectionDiagram.summary: 60-second XID-age telemetry catches wraparound hours early, while single-user VACUUM FREEZE provides deterministic recovery.
sectionDiagram.caption: 60s telemetry alerts at 500M XIDs to prevent hitting the 1.997B read-only wall requiring single-user VACUUM FREEZE.

knowledgeChecks.question: In Production Scenario #28, which two factors combined to push the 400 GB ledger into an XID wraparound write freeze?

options.text: An idle `BEGIN; SELECT` transaction pinning `xmin` and default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` throttling vacuum behind 30K updates/sec.
options.feedback: Correct. Pinned xmin blocked dead-tuple cleanup (5x bloat) while default cost_limit=200 couldn't keep pace with 30K XIDs/sec.
Incorrect. Those are the hardened fixes, not the cause.

options.text: Using weekly range partitions on the ledger table.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Weekly partitioning reduces vacuum blast radius.
Incorrect. Larger maintenance_work_mem speeds up VACUUM index passes.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A pinned xmin horizon from an idle reporting transaction plus throttled default autovacuum (cost_limit=200) caused 5x bloat and XID wraparound.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if an orphaned replication slot stays `active=false` with `hot_standby_feedback=on` and no `max_slot_keep_wal_size`?

options.text: PostgreSQL automatically drops the slot after 30 seconds.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Without max_slot_keep_wal_size, PostgreSQL retains WAL and xmin indefinitely.

options.text: The dead slot pins `xmin`/`catalog_xmin` and retains WAL on disk until autovacuum starves or the disk fills.
options.feedback: Correct. Setting max_slot_keep_wal_size bounds WAL retention and invalidates dead slots before they cause an outage.

options.text: HOT updates convert into sequential scans.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Dead slots affect WAL retention and xmin horizon, not query planner scans directly.
Incorrect. relfrozenxid only advances when VACUUM freezes old tuples.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: An inactive replication slot with hot_standby_feedback pins xmin and retains WAL until max_slot_keep_wal_size invalidates it.

knowledgeChecks.question: If a PostgreSQL cluster has already hit the emergency read-only XID wraparound shutdown, what is the standard recovery procedure?

options.feedback: Incorrect. Normal multi-user mode refuses writes until XIDs are frozen.

options.text: Stop client pools, launch `postgres --single` mode, run `VACUUM FREEZE;` on the affected database, and restart.
options.feedback: Correct. Single-user mode bypasses the multi-user write lock solely to run VACUUM FREEZE and advance datfrozenxid.

options.text: Delete `pg_wal` files manually to reset the XID counter.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Deleting pg_wal corrupts the database and causes data loss.

options.text: Run `REINDEX DATABASE` from a read-only replica.
options.feedback: Incorrect. REINDEX does not freeze heap tuple XIDs.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Recovery from a wraparound shutdown requires starting PostgreSQL in single-user mode (`postgres --single`) and executing `VACUUM FREEZE`.

beginner.summary: Stop PostgreSQL write freezes by killing idle transactions after 30 seconds, leaving 30% free space on data pages, and letting autovacuum run faster.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Short idle-transaction timeouts and faster autovacuum prevent table bloat and emergency database shutdowns.
beginner.byteSummary:
When a busy database updates 30,000 rows per second, autovacuum needs to clean up old row versions continuously. If an idle query blocks cleanup, the table grows 5x larger and the database eventually stops writes to protect data.

Adding a 30-second timeout on idle transactions and boosting autovacuum speed keeps the database healthy.

intermediate.summary: Combine fillfactor=70 HOT updates, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s, max_slot_keep_wal_size, and autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000 to hold bloat < 5%.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Unpinning xmin and raising autovacuum I/O budget 10x prevents wraparound outages on 30K updates/sec ledgers.
intermediate.byteSummary:
To protect a 400 GB ledger at 30,000 updates/sec, enforce `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s` and `max_slot_keep_wal_size` so no session or dead replica pins `xmin`.

Use `fillfactor=70` for page-local HOT updates and raise `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000` so freeze workers outpace XID consumption.

advanced.summary: Production hardening pairs HOT fillfactor=70, 30s idle-in-tx timeouts, cost_limit=2000, weekly range partitioning, zero-SAVEPOINT hygiene, and 60s XID-age alerting.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Weekly partitioning shrinks freeze scans from 400 GB to 20 GB (~4.3 min), while 500M XID alerts leave hours of runway before single-user VACUUM FREEZE.
advanced.byteSummary:
Beyond `fillfactor=70`, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s`, and `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000`, weekly range partitioning isolates 20 GB hot writes from 380 GB all-frozen cold partitions (4.3-minute freeze sweeps) and eliminating `SAVEPOINT` loops prevents SubtransSLRU XID amplification.

Continuous 60s `datfrozenxid` telemetry alerts at 150M/500M/1.5B XIDs long before `postgres --single` `VACUUM FREEZE` is ever needed.
